about.text: The Corsican counterpart of Sardinian casu martzu, made especially in villages of southern Corsica: a cheese left open to cheese flies (Piophila casei), whose larvae break it down until it is very soft and pungent.

sources.text: The photograph, its author and its licence, from its page.

how.label: lure the fly
how.text: A whole Corsican sheep's- or goat's-milk tomme is left where cheese flies can lay their eggs; the larvae feeding inside break the paste down into a very soft, tunnelled mass that weeps a liquid called 'lagrima'.

steps.note: Matured in an airy place open to flies, which lay eggs on the tomme.
